title: pkg/registry/ structure and how services enter the boot sequence
answers: How do registry.apis and registry.apps differ?
Where do background services get collected at startup?
body:
pkg/registry/ is composition/wiring code, not business logic. Three sub-registries feed pkg/server at boot:
- apis/ (pkg apiregistry): k8s-style API group builders (folders, dashboards, iam, provisioning, secrets, ...) implementing builder.APIGroupBuilder.
- apps/ (pkg appregistry): newer App-SDK based apps (playlist, shorturl, quotas, ...) wrapped as appsdkapiserver.AppInstaller.
- backgroundsvcs/ + usagestatssvcs/: flat lists of everything implementing registry.BackgroundService / registry.ProvidesUsageStats (defined in pkg/registry/registry.go).
Actual REST storage/conversion/validation logic lives in the builder's own subpackage (apis/folders/*.go, apps/playlist/migrator/) or in apps/<name>/pkg/..., not in the registration file itself.
